title: Folding & State Aggregation (lists:foldl/3 vs. lists:foldr/3)
solutionExplanation: Demonstrates tail-recursive state aggregation using lists:foldl/3 with multi-accumulator tuples and list inversion patterns.

otpDocCards.description: Calls Fun(Elem, AccIn) on successive elements of List, left to right. Strictly tail-recursive.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why does lists:foldl(fun(Elem, Acc) -> [Elem | Acc] end, [], [1, 2, 3]) return [3, 2, 1] instead of [1, 2, 3]?

options.label: Because foldl visits elements from left to right, prepending each new element onto the head of the accumulator list (LIFO stack behavior)
options.explanation: 1 is prepended -> [1]; then 2 is prepended -> [2, 1]; then 3 is prepended -> [3, 2, 1].

options.label: Because the BEAM VM reverses lists internally before evaluating foldl
options.explanation: foldl processes the input list in its original forward order; prepending to the head of a singly linked list is what reverses the order.

options.label: Because foldl is body-recursive and unwinds the stack backwards
options.explanation: foldl is strictly tail-recursive, not body-recursive.
